reportMarkdown:
## Direct write for awaited calls, judged on the loopback bench Finished

**Index:** 13 · **Checkpoint:** b0063b5 · **Result Commit:** ba25d5f · **Attempt Count:** 1

**Passed Status:** true. Invocation round trips 19% faster on the loopback bench for both protocols, sends within the 3% bar (+2.5%), Aspire invoke p50 -4% to -6% with 34% less CPU per call, and no regression elsewhere. Unit tests (497 + 546), fmt, clippy, both wasm checks and 32 native end-to-end cells (invoke, send, server-stream, graceful-stop, executor-independence, server-close, ordinary-reconnect, concurrency-and-clones, callback-dispatch, client-result-errors, message-burst, stream-cancellation, client-to-server-stream, keepalive-idle, disconnect-every-handle, restart-after-stop, large-payload) pass. The architecture chapter describes the direct write.

**Scope lock:** the experiment 10 patch, unchanged, plus its architecture paragraph.

**Finding:** experiments 4–11 were decided on an instrument too coarse for the fire-and-forget side effect; the loopback bench shows that side effect is +2.5% per send, while the round-trip gain is 19%.
